text:
Maria: heads-up: ran a long-context perf sweep comparing KV reuse on hosted, dedicated, and our onprem VPC. something weird with heatmap sampling and page residency.

Ajay: paste the numbers pls

Maria: short: for steady 16k token stream, hosted RSS stabilizes ~55GB, dedicated ~72GB, private(onprem) ~88GB. fragmentation score much higher on private. batching config identical.

Devon: that's a big delta. same model + quant + batch settings?

Maria: yes. model build is llama-like opt-quant, fp16 with 8-bit kv quant. config we used:
```
kv_cache:
  max_slots: 1000000
  page_size: 2MB
  eviction_policy: lru
batching:
  max_tokens: 2048
  max_batch_size: 32
```

Sophie: what about hugepages / jemalloc / kernel flags across the envs?

Maria: hosted = default cloud image (THP enabled), dedicated = GCE reserved with THP=always, onprem = hugetlbfs disabled + jemalloc custom flags (older infra image). suspect page alignment / MTU interaction.

Ajay: could MTU affect page fragmentation?

Maria: yes 97 in private we see a lot of small allocations due to 1MB hugepage shortage; kernel falls back to memcpy kernels for kv copy at long sequence lengths. Logs show page splits.

Devon: got a flamegraph or heatmap? even ascii helps.

Maria: heatmap excerpt (rows=time, cols=kv-page-id):
```
hosted:  \u2591\u2591\u2591\u2591\u2591\u2591\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2591\u2591\u2591\u2591

dedicated: \u2591\u2591\u2591\u2591\u2591\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2591

private:  \u2591\u2591\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593\u2593
```
(interpretation: private shows denser hot pages but a long sparse tail -> higher fragmentation)

Sophie: did kernel selection logs show fallback? where are those printed?

Maria: runtime logs: 
```
[2026-02-12T14:02:03Z] kernel_selector: using auto (AVX2) -> selected cu_memcpy_fallback due to page alignment mismatch
[2026-02-12T14:02:03Z] kv_cache: page_split_detected page_id=842 size_before=2MB size_after=256KB
```

Ajay: page_split_detected is new (we added detection in rc). may be jemalloc mapping causing it. repro script?

Maria: repro: continuous 16k prompt loops + monitor /proc/<pid>/smaps and runtime evict counters. run flags:
```
./run_infer --model res/17b --tokens 16000 --loop 1000 --kv-warmup=enabled
```

Devon: eviction counters?

Maria: hosted evict_count ~1200, dedicated ~4200, private ~13800 across same workload. private evicts skew to many small evicts (<=64KB).

Sophie: small evicts -> fragmentation -> more evicts -> more memcpy -> latency tail.

Maria: exactly. p50 per-token gen: hosted 38ms, dedicated 45ms, private 78ms. p95 private spikes >200ms at splits.

Ajay: does batching heuristic amplify KV pressure? e.g., increasing max_batch_size could worsen it?

Maria: we tested max_batch_size 32 -> 64: hosted slightly improved, dedicated slightly worse, private got catastrophic (OOM aborts). allocator on private couldn't coalesce frames.

Devon: mitigation ideas? eviction_policy=lfu or coalesce_window tweaks?

Maria: quick experiment: eviction_policy='threshold-coalesce' reduced private evict_count 13800->3800, p50->56ms, p95->110ms. good improvement.

Sophie: long-term: standardize jemalloc flags + enable THP and hugetlb reservation on private images. kernel patch to avoid page_split when copying between non-aligned pages would help too.

Ajay: any security/VPC reasons we can't change kernel params on customers' private images?

Maria: yes, many customers lock images. will need opt-in image upgrades. fallback: runtime should detect split-heavy envs and fall back to smaller page_size (256KB) to avoid splits.

Devon: idea: runtime heatmap sampling could proactively remap hot pages to contiguous hugetlb-backed segments when available.

Maria: will prototype. filing a short RFC + perf PR with experiments. also adding a diagnostic endpoint:
```
/diag/kv_heatmap -> { hot_pages: 123, frag_score: 0.72, evict_small_pct: 0.87 }
```

Ajay: include SRE/OnPrem runbook one-liner please.

Maria: one-liner:
```
curl http://localhost:8080/diag/kv_heatmap | jq
```

Sophie: thanks 97 please cc eng-sre and eng-infra on RFC. looks like config drift + kernel/allocator differences not model regression.

Maria: filing now, attaching logs and repro. tagging @dev-oncall for potential maintenance window :wave:

Dev-oncall: got it, will coordinate maintenance window if needed :thumbsup:
